name: TGF-beta growth factor serums
lead: TGF-beta growth factor serums are topical skincare products that contain transforming growth factor beta, often alongside other growth factors, in a cosmetic base. People use them to make skin look firmer and smoother, with the stated goal of encouraging the skin's collagen-producing cells.

Many such serums source their growth factors from cultured skin cells or their conditioned medium. They are sold as cosmetics; the FDA states that US law does not recognize 'cosmeceuticals' as a category and that a product with drug properties must be approved as a drug [1]. Published trials on specific serums are limited.

chain: Serum delivers growth factors to the skin surface
Signals aimed at fibroblasts and collagen production
Skin looks firmer with finer lines
angle.text: Users apply these serums daily to improve fine lines, texture and firmness. They are often used after microneedling or in-clinic procedures, in a skin-rejuvenation routine.

paras: Growth factor serums are used on the face for anti-aging, texture and post-procedure skin care. TGF-beta is the factor most linked to collagen synthesis in skin biology, which is the basis for its inclusion.

Proponents say topical TGF-beta signals fibroblasts to make collagen and other matrix proteins. Whether large protein molecules reach the dermis through intact skin is discussed by formulators, and some products pair them with microneedling to improve delivery.

Wikipedia notes that in the US cosmetic products have no legal requirement to prove their claims, and that the term cosmeceutical can lead consumers to assume drug-level testing [1]. TGF-beta also plays roles in scarring biology, and users commonly patch test new serums.

card.summary: Topical serums containing TGF-beta and other growth factors that people use to make skin look firmer and smoother.
card.note: Sold as cosmetics; claims are not pre-approved by regulators.

quick.overview:
These serums put growth factors, including TGF-beta, in a skincare product. People apply them to improve firmness, texture and fine lines.

They are often used after microneedling or procedures as part of a rejuvenation routine.
quick.mechanism: Proponents say TGF-beta signals fibroblasts to produce collagen. Delivery through intact skin is a topic formulators discuss.
quick.risks: They are cosmetics, so claims are not pre-approved [1]. Irritation is possible; patch testing is commonly recommended on labels.
